html:
Helike was a Greek city in Achaea, on the north coast of the Peloponnese near the Gulf of Corinth, that was destroyed in one winter night in 373 BCE by an earthquake and a wave from the sea.

It was a leading city of the Achaean League and home to a famous sanctuary of Poseidon, god of the sea and of earthquakes. Ancient writers say the ground shook, the city sank and the sea poured in, killing everyone. Many Greeks took it as Poseidon's punishment. For centuries visitors said they could see the ruins under the water, and the drowned city became a legend. Some scholars think it helped inspire Plato's story of Atlantis, written a few years later.

Modern research explains it as an earthquake that dropped the coast, followed by a tsunami, much like the Malian Gulf tsunami described by Thucydides. In 2001 archaeologists found remains of the classical city buried on land under the sediments of an old lagoon, not in the open sea.
sum: Helike was a Greek city in Achaea, on the north coast of the Peloponnese near the Gulf of Corinth, that was destroyed in one winter night in 373 BCE by an earthquake and a wave from the sea.
